name: Octinoxate
summary: The common organic UVB filter in sunscreens and lip balms, absorbed into the blood and flagged for endocrine activity in lab work, yet judged safe at 10% by the EU's SCCS in 2025.
lead: Octinoxate (octyl methoxycinnamate, ethylhexyl methoxycinnamate, OMC) is an organic UVB filter used in sunscreens, lip balms and cosmetics with SPF claims . It absorbs UVB with a peak near 310 nm and is typically combined with other filters .

name: Oxybenzone
summary: A broad-spectrum sunscreen filter found in most people's urine, linked to reef-damage findings and banned in places like Hawaii, yet still legal under US federal rules.
lead: Oxybenzone (benzophenone-3, BP-3) is an organic UV filter that absorbs UVB and short-wave UVA, used in sunscreens, lip products, hair sprays, nail polish and as a stabiliser in plastics . It was first synthesised in 1906 by Bernhard König and Stanisław Kostanecki and later developed as a sunscreen ingredient from the 1950s, according to Grokipedia .

name: Octisalate
summary: A weak UVB filter used mostly to lift SPF and steady other filters; absorbed through skin in small amounts and under European endocrine testing requirements.
lead: Octisalate (octyl salicylate, 2-ethylhexyl salicylate) is an ester of salicylic acid used in sunscreens and cosmetics as a weak UVB absorber, usually added to boost SPF and to help stabilise other filters such as avobenzone and oxybenzone . It is also an emollient that adds water resistance .

name: Homosalate
summary: A common UVB sunscreen filter whose possible hormone-like activity has led to EU concentration limits and animal-testing demands; human harm has not been shown.
lead: Homosalate (3,3,5-trimethylcyclohexyl salicylate) is a salicylate ester used as an organic UVB filter in sunscreens and SPF cosmetics . It absorbs UVB at roughly 295-315 nm and is reported to be found in about 45% of US sunscreens .

name: Ensulizole
summary: A water-soluble UVB sunscreen filter for light facial lotions; evidence is sunscreen-class, not appearance-specific.
lead: Ensulizole, also known as phenylbenzimidazole sulfonic acid (PBSA) and 2-phenylbenzimidazole-5-sulfonic acid, is a water-soluble organic ultraviolet (UV) filter used in sunscreens and daily facial moisturisers. It is primarily a UVB absorber with minimal UVA coverage, so it is generally combined with other filters when broad-spectrum protection is intended.

name: Ecamsule
summary: L'Oreal's photostable UVA filter, Mexoryl SX; established in sunscreens abroad, US-approved only via NDA products.
lead: Ecamsule, sold under the trade name Mexoryl SX and known by the INCI name terephthalylidene dicamphor sulfonic acid, is a photostable organic UVA filter developed and patented by L'Oreal in 1982. It absorbs ultraviolet light between roughly 290 and 400 nm, with a peak near 345 nm, and is typically combined with other filters (such as avobenzone and octocrylene) because it does not cover the whole UV range on its own.

name: Bemotrizinol
summary: A photostable broad-spectrum UV filter long used in EU, Australian and Asian sunscreens and reportedly newly cleared in the US.
lead: Bemotrizinol (INCI: bis-ethylhexyloxyphenol methoxyphenyl triazine, BEMT; trade names Tinosorb S, Escalol S, Parsol Shield) is an oil-soluble organic UV filter that absorbs both UVB and UVA, with absorption peaks around 310 and 340-345 nm. It is noted for photostability and for helping stabilise less stable filters such as avobenzone.

name: Bisoctrizole
summary: A particle-form UV filter (Tinosorb M) that covers UVA and UVB; common abroad, not US-approved.
lead: Bisoctrizole (INCI: methylene bis-benzotriazolyl tetramethylbutylphenol, MBBT; trade names Tinosorb M, Parsol Max) is a phenolic bis-benzotriazole UV absorber used in sunscreens. It is made as microfine particles, usually supplied as a roughly 50% aqueous suspension, and is described as a hybrid between organic and particulate filters.

name: Diethylamino hydroxybenzoyl hexyl benzoate
summary: A photostable UVA sunscreen filter common outside the US; evidence is lab-based and regulatory.
lead: Diethylamino hydroxybenzoyl hexyl benzoate (DHHB), sold as Uvinul A Plus (BASF) and Parsol DHHB (DSM), is an oil-soluble organic UVA filter with an absorption maximum near 354 nm, noted for photostability and compatibility with other UV absorbers.

name: Ethylhexyl triazone
summary: A highly photostable UVB filter used in high-SPF products abroad; no clinical trials of it alone.
lead: Ethylhexyl triazone (octyl triazone, EHT; Uvinul T 150 from BASF, Parsol EHT from DSM-Firmenich) is an oil-soluble organic UVB filter with an absorption maximum near 314 nm. Its structure is a triazine ring bearing three 2-ethylhexyl benzoate groups.

name: Drometrizole trisiloxane
summary: Photostable L'Oreal UVA/UVB sunscreen filter (Mexoryl XL), approved in the EU and elsewhere but not in the US.
lead: Drometrizole trisiloxane (INCI name; sold by L'Oreal as Mexoryl XL, also called silatrizole) is a lipophilic benzotriazole-derived organic ultraviolet filter used in sunscreens and daily-wear skincare products . It is described as a broad-spectrum absorber with peaks near 303 nm (UVB) and 344 nm (UVA) and is frequently formulated together with ecamsule (Mexoryl SX) .

name: Enzacamene
summary: Camphor-derived UVB sunscreen filter (4-MBC) now banned in EU cosmetics over endocrine-activity findings.
lead: Enzacamene (4-methylbenzylidene camphor, 4-MBC) is a camphor-derived organic UVB filter that has been used in sunscreens and SPF-labelled skincare . It has been the subject of endocrine-activity research, and it has been banned in cosmetics in the European Union (Regulation (EU) 2024/996), with further bans reported in the UK and China .

name: Amiloxate
summary: Cinnamate UVB sunscreen filter approved in the EU since 1997; photoallergy case reports exist and little else is studied.
lead: Amiloxate (isoamyl p-methoxycinnamate, isopentyl 4-methoxycinnamate, IMC) is a cinnamate ester used as a UVB filter in sunscreen products . It has been approved in the European Union since 1997; in the United States it has been under regulatory evaluation rather than listed as an approved sunscreen active .

name: Bisdisulizole disodium
summary: Water-soluble UVA sunscreen filter (Neo Heliopan AP), EU-approved since 2000 and not approved in the US.
lead: Bisdisulizole disodium (trade name Neo Heliopan AP, from Symrise; also abbreviated DPDT) is a water-soluble organic UVA filter used in sunscreens . It is a disodium salt with two sulfonated benzimidazole units on a phenylene core .

name: Meradimate
summary: Older US-listed anthranilate UVA sunscreen filter, studied mostly for its photophysics.
lead: Meradimate (menthyl anthranilate) is an ester of anthranilic acid and menthol that acts as a UVA filter in sunscreens . It is one of the 17 ingredients the US FDA lists for over-the-counter sunscreen products . It should not be confused with methyl anthranilate .

name: Padimate O
summary: Older PABA-derived UVB filter, now rarely used, with mixed lab data on photochemistry.
lead: Padimate O (octyl dimethyl PABA, 2-ethylhexyl 4-dimethylaminobenzoate, sold as Escalol 507) is an oily, water-insoluble ester related to PABA that has been used as a UVB filter in sunscreens and lip products . It is approved by one or more agencies including the US FDA, per Wikipedia .

name: PABA
summary: The original UVB sunscreen filter, largely dropped over allergy, staining and phototoxicity concerns.
lead: PABA (para-aminobenzoic acid, 4-aminobenzoic acid) is a small aromatic compound with an amino group and a carboxyl group on opposite sides of a benzene ring. It occurs naturally in foods such as liver, brewer's yeast, mushrooms and whole grains, and is an intermediate in folate synthesis in bacteria, plants and fungi. In appearance culture it is known as one of the first active ingredients used in sunscreens.

name: Cinoxate
summary: An older cinnamate UVB filter, approved in the US in 1961 and now rarely used.
lead: Cinoxate is an organic UVB filter, an ester of methoxycinnamic acid and 2-ethoxyethanol, used in some sunscreen formulations. According to Wikipedia, the US FDA approved it as a UV filter in 1961, and a 2023 review cited there describes it as no longer commonly used in cosmetic formulations.

name: Dioxybenzone
summary: A benzophenone UVB/short-UVA sunscreen filter listed in the US monograph, with almost no dedicated research.
lead: Dioxybenzone, also called benzophenone-8, is a benzophenone-derived sunscreen ingredient that absorbs UVB and short-wave UVA light. Chemically it is (2-hydroxy-4-methoxyphenyl)(2-hydroxyphenyl)methanone, a yellow powder that is insoluble in water.

name: Sulisobenzone
summary: A water-soluble benzophenone UV filter (BP-4) used in sunscreens and hair products, studied mostly as an environmental contaminant.
lead: Sulisobenzone, or benzophenone-4, is a water-soluble benzophenone UV filter that protects against UVB and short-wave UVA light. Its sodium salt is called benzophenone-5. It is used in some sunscreens and, per its cosmetic ingredient listing, in hair products to protect colour and structure.

name: Trolamine salicylate
summary: A weak salicylate UVB filter better known as the active in odourless muscle-pain creams.
lead: Trolamine salicylate (triethanolamine salicylate) is a salt of triethanolamine and salicylic acid used in over-the-counter topical pain-relief creams such as Aspercreme, and historically as a weak UVB absorber in sunscreens and cosmetics. The salicylate absorbs UVB, the triethanolamine neutralises acidity, and the compound is odourless, unlike menthol-based rubs.

name: Polysilicone-15
summary: A silicone-polymer UVB filter (Parsol SLX) used in sunscreens, lip balms and hair products, with only case-report safety data.
lead: Polysilicone-15 (dimethicodiethylbenzalmalonate; trade name Parsol SLX, from DSM) is a siloxane-based oligomer used as a UVB filter, with peak absorption near 310 nm. It is a colourless to pale-yellow liquid, practically insoluble in water. It is approved for sunscreens and cosmetics in the EU, and appears in hair products such as shampoos, sprays and colour treatments. It also appears in US-listed lip-balm sunscreens combined with other filters.

name: Tris-biphenyl triazine
summary: Newer particulate UV filter (Tinosorb A2B); only lab and formulation research exists, with no human trials.
lead: Tris-biphenyl triazine (TBPT), marketed under the trade name Tinosorb A2B, is a synthetic ultraviolet (UV) filter used in sunscreen and daily-wear skincare products. It belongs to the triazine family of filters, which also includes bemotrizinol (Tinosorb S) and phenylene bis-diphenyltriazine .

name: Methoxypropylamino cyclohexenylidene ethoxyethylcyanoacetate
summary: L'Oreal's UVA1 filter (Mexoryl 400 / UVMune), EU-approved in 2019 with no published human trials.
lead: Methoxypropylamino cyclohexenylidene ethoxyethylcyanoacetate (abbreviated MCE) is an organic UV filter used in sunscreens to absorb long-wave UVA radiation. According to Wikipedia it was developed by L'Oreal and BASF, and L'Oreal markets it as Mexoryl 400, while its subsidiary La Roche-Posay sells it as UVMune .

name: Phenylene bis-diphenyltriazine
summary: Newer triazine UV filter (TriAsorB) pitched as covering blue light too; evidence is mostly developer-authored.
lead: Phenylene bis-diphenyltriazine (PBDT), also known as TriAsorB, is a synthetic UV filter that absorbs UVB and UVA radiation and, according to its developers, also high-energy visible (blue) light . It is a triazine-class filter, listed alongside bemotrizinol and tris-biphenyl triazine in ingredient tables .

name: Titanium dioxide
summary: The classic mineral UV filter and white pigment in physical sunscreens and tinted SPF; broad but weaker on UVA I.
lead: Titanium dioxide (TiO2), also called titanium white or CI 77891, is a white, water-insoluble mineral compound and the most widely used white pigment. It is found in paints, plastics, paper and toothpaste as well as cosmetics . In skincare it serves as a mineral (physical) UV filter and as a pigment in tinted products.

name: Zinc oxide
summary: Mineral UV filter and skin protectant with broad UVA/UVB coverage; also the base of diaper-rash and barrier creams.
lead: Zinc oxide (ZnO) is an inorganic white powder used as a mineral UV filter in sunscreens and as a skin protectant in diaper-rash creams, barrier ointments and calamine lotion . Wikipedia calls it the broadest-spectrum UVA and UVB absorber among sunscreen filters and states it is completely photostable .

name: Nano zinc oxide
summary: Nanoparticle zinc oxide: the invisible-on-skin version of the mineral filter, with debate centred on penetration and aquatic toxicity.
lead: Nano zinc oxide refers to zinc oxide particles in the nanometre size range, used in sunscreens and other personal-care products as a mineral UV filter. Grokipedia states that the small size permits higher loadings without the white cast of larger particles, and that particles are often silica-coated to limit reactivity on skin .

name: Nano titanium dioxide
summary: Sheer, nanoscale mineral UV filter used in modern sunscreens; protection is well established for the category but the nano-specific safety debate continues.
lead: Nano titanium dioxide (nano-TiO2) refers to engineered particles of titanium dioxide, typically 1 to 100 nanometres across, that absorb ultraviolet light while remaining largely transparent in visible light. In sunscreens they are used as a mineral UV filter, often alongside ultrafine zinc oxide, to reduce sunburn and long-term sun damage. The smaller particle size is the reason such formulations can look sheer on the skin rather than leaving the opaque white cast associated with older mineral products.

name: Cerium oxide
summary: Industrial ceramic oxide floated as a low-photoreactivity mineral UV absorber; antioxidant nanoceria research exists, sunscreen evidence does not.
lead: Cerium oxide (cerium(IV) oxide, ceria, CeO2) is a pale yellow-white, water-insoluble ceramic powder with a cubic fluorite crystal structure. It is mainly an industrial material, used for glass polishing, glass decolourising, catalysts including automotive catalytic converters, and fuel cells. In cosmetics discussions it appears as a candidate mineral UV absorber; Wikipedia describes nanoceria as a prospective replacement for zinc oxide and titanium dioxide in sunscreens because of lower photocatalytic activity.
